title: Zaru soba
summary: Chilled buckwheat noodles served with a savoury soy-dashi dipping sauce, spring onions and wasabi.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
method: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes, then chill for at least 30 minutes until completely cold.
Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips. Fill a large bowl with cold water and ice.
Boil the soba in a large pot over high heat for 4–6 minutes, until tender with a slight bite.
Drain, then rinse under cold water, rubbing gently, until the water runs clear and the noodles are cold. Plunge into the iced water for 30 seconds and drain well.
Divide the noodles among 4 plates or trays and top with the nori. Serve the chilled sauce in small bowls, with the spring onions and wasabi to stir in before dipping.

stages.title: Make the dipping sauce
steps: Combine the dashi stock, soy sauce and mirin in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat and cook for 2 minutes to cook off the alcohol in the mirin.
Pour the sauce into a heatproof bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Chill the sauce and prepare the garnishes
steps: Cover the sauce and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until completely cold.
While the sauce chills, thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips with scissors.
Fill a large bowl with cold water and plenty of ice, ready for the noodles.

stages.title: Cook and rinse the noodles
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil over high heat. Add the soba noodles and stir straight away so the strands do not stick together.
Cook according to the packet, usually 4–6 minutes, until tender but still with a slight bite.
Drain in a colander and rinse under cold running water, rubbing the noodles gently with your hands, until the water runs clear and the noodles are cold.
Plunge the noodles into the iced water for 30 seconds, then drain very well.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the noodles among 4 plates or bamboo trays and scatter the nori strips on top.
Pour the chilled sauce into 4 small bowls and place the spring onions and wasabi alongside.
To eat, stir wasabi and spring onions into the sauce, then dip a few noodles at a time.

tips: Rinsing the noodles under cold water and rubbing them removes surface starch, which stops them turning gluey and clumping.
The ice bath chills the noodles quickly and firms them, giving the chewy texture zaru soba is known for.
Chill the sauce fully, as warm sauce softens the noodles and dulls the wasabi.
Soba brands vary in cooking time, so taste a strand a minute before the packet time is up.
variations: Serve the sauce with a little grated ginger and a pinch of toasted sesame seeds alongside the spring onions.
Use the same sauce with chilled udon noodles instead of soba. Check the label if you need a wheat-free soba, as many contain wheat flour.
storage: Eat the noodles straight away. Keep leftover dipping sauce in a covered container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Aloo paratha
summary: Golden wholewheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes, crisp outside and soft within.
ingredients: 300 g wholewheat atta flour, plus 1/4 cup extra for rolling
450 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
method: Mix the atta flour, half the salt and 180 ml water into a soft dough. Knead for 3–4 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam-dry for 5 minutes.
Mash the potatoes smooth, then mix in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and remaining salt. Cool for 5 minutes and roll into 6 balls.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Flatten each, enclose a potato ball, seal well, then roll into an 18 cm round using the extra flour for dusting.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Cook each paratha for 1 minute until pale spots appear, then flip and brush with melted butter.
Cook 30–60 seconds each side, brushing the other side with butter, until golden brown with darker spots. Keep wrapped in a tea towel and serve hot.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the atta flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add 180 ml water, mixing with your hand until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a bench for 3–4 minutes until smooth and supple, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Rest the dough for 20 minutes, which relaxes the gluten so the parathas roll without tearing.

stages.title: Cook and season the potato filling
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and leave in the colander for 5 minutes so the steam escapes.
Mash the potatoes until completely smooth, then stir in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Cool the filling for 5 minutes, then roll it into 6 equal balls.

stages.title: Stuff and roll the parathas
steps: Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a 9 cm round, using a little of the extra flour for dusting.
Place a potato ball in the centre, pull the edges up around it and pinch together to seal fully.
Flatten the sealed ball gently, then roll with light pressure into an 18 cm round, dusting with flour as needed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling, stacking the rolled parathas with baking paper or flour between them.

stages.title: Cook the parathas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan or flat skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until hot.
Cook one paratha for 1 minute, until small bubbles appear and the underside has pale spots, then flip.
Brush the top with some of the melted butter and cook for 1 minute, then flip and brush the other side.
Cook for a further 30–60 seconds each side, pressing gently with a spatula, until both sides are golden brown with darker spots.
Keep the cooked parathas wrapped in a clean tea towel while you cook the rest, then serve hot.

tips: Mash the potatoes until there are no lumps and let them cool; a wet or lumpy filling splits the dough when rolling.
Seal the dough completely around the filling, because any gap lets the potato leak out and burn in the pan.
Dust with only as much flour as needed, since excess flour scorches in the pan and tastes bitter.
Cook over medium-high heat so the parathas brown and cook through quickly; a low heat dries them out and makes them tough.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp ground turmeric and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the filling for a more fiery, golden paratha.
Mix 60 g crumbled paneer into the mashed potato for a richer, creamier filling.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze with baking paper between layers for up to 1 month. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes each side until hot through.

title: Revithada
summary: Chickpeas slowly baked with onion, bay leaf and lemon until creamy in a fragrant olive-oil broth.
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, plus extra to taste
method: Soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 8 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse well.
Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Put the chickpeas, onions, bay leaves, half the olive oil and 1 litre water in a heavy lidded casserole.
Bring to the boil on the stovetop over medium-high heat, then simmer gently about 5 minutes, skimming the foam until little new foam forms.
Cover and bake for 3 hours, until the chickpeas crush easily. Top up with boiling water if they poke out.
Discard the bay leaves, then stir in the salt, pepper, lemon juice and remaining olive oil. Mash a handful of chickpeas until the broth turns thick and creamy.
Rest, covered, for 15 minutes, then taste and add more salt if needed.

stages.title: Soak the chickpeas
steps: Place the dried chickpeas in a large bowl and cover with cold water by about 10 cm, as they will swell to double their size.
Leave to soak at room temperature for 8 hours or overnight.
Drain the chickpeas in a colander and rinse well under cold running water.

stages.title: Assemble the casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan).
Thinly slice the onions.
Put the drained chickpeas, onions, bay leaves and half the olive oil (50 ml) into a large heavy casserole dish with a tight-fitting lid.
Pour in 1 litre water, which should cover the chickpeas by about 3 cm.

stages.title: Bring to the boil
steps: Set the casserole over medium-high heat on the stovetop and bring to the boil, about 5 minutes.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and skim off the white foam from the surface for about 5 minutes, until little new foam forms.

stages.title: Bake until tender
steps: Cover the casserole with the lid and transfer to the oven.
Bake for 3 hours, until the chickpeas are completely tender and crush easily between your fingers.
Check the liquid after 1½ hours and again near the end. If the chickpeas are poking out, top up with boiling water so they stay just covered.
Do not add salt during baking, as it can keep the chickpeas firm.

stages.title: Season and rest
steps: Remove the casserole from the oven and discard the bay leaves.
Stir in the salt, a good grind of black pepper, the lemon juice and the remaining 50 ml olive oil.
Mash a handful of chickpeas against the side of the dish with a spoon for about 1 minute, until the broth turns thick and creamy like a loose stew.
Rest, covered, for 15 minutes, then taste and add more salt if needed before serving.

tips: Soaking the chickpeas overnight gives even cooking and a creamy centre, so they don't split before the middles soften.
Add salt only once the chickpeas are tender, because salting early can toughen their skins.
Slow baking in a tightly lidded pot makes a thick, silky broth without stirring, and the oil emulsifies with the starch released by the chickpeas.
Stirring in lemon juice after baking keeps its flavour bright, as long cooking would dull it.
variations: Add 1 tsp dried oregano and a sprig of rosemary with the bay leaves for a more herbal broth.
Stir in a few handfuls of baby spinach after baking and let it wilt in the hot broth for 2–3 minutes.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat with a splash of water until piping hot.

title: Kongnamul guk
summary: A light, clean-tasting soybean sprout soup simmered with garlic, spring onion and anchovy broth.
ingredients: 1/4 tsp salt, plus extra to taste
method: Rinse the soybean sprouts, discarding any slimy or discoloured ones and loose husks. Finely chop the garlic and thinly slice the spring onions.
Bring the vegetable stock to the boil in a medium saucepan over high heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the sprouts and garlic, cover and reduce to medium heat. Simmer for 7 minutes without lifting the lid, until tender with a little crunch.
Stir in the soy sauce and salt, then simmer uncovered for 2 minutes. Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Stir in the spring onions and sesame oil, then turn off the heat. Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

stages.title: Prepare the sprouts and aromatics
steps: Rinse the soybean sprouts in cold water, drain well and discard any slimy or discoloured sprouts and loose bean husks.
Finely chop the garlic.
Thinly slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts together.

stages.title: Simmer the sprouts
steps: Pour the vegetable stock into a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat, about 5 minutes.
Add the sprouts and garlic, then cover with the lid and reduce the heat to medium.
Simmer, covered, for 7 minutes without lifting the lid, which keeps the beany smell from developing, until the sprouts are tender but still have a little crunch.

stages.title: Season and finish
steps: Stir in the soy sauce and the salt, then simmer uncovered over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Stir in the spring onions and sesame oil and turn off the heat.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot as a side with other dishes.

tips: Keep the lid on for the first cook: lifting it early can leave a raw, grassy bean smell in the soup.
Don't overcook the sprouts, as they lose their crunch within a few minutes of the recommended time.
Add the sesame oil at the end because heat dulls its nutty aroma.
Use a vegetable stock that tastes good on its own, as the soup is mostly broth.
variations: For a spicy version, add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic.
For a hangover-style soup, add a handful of sliced kimchi with the sprouts and omit the soy sauce if the kimchi is salty.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat until just hot, as boiling makes the sprouts soft. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Arroz chaufa
summary: Peruvian-Chinese fried rice with chicken, eggs, spring onions and a deeply savoury soy glaze.
ingredients: 300 g chicken thigh, cut into 1 cm pieces
4 spring onions, whites and greens separated, thinly sliced
method: Break up the cold rice. Toss the chicken with the salt and pepper. Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil together, and keep the spring onion whites and greens separate.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering. Scramble the eggs for 30–40 seconds until just set, then break up and set aside.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in the wok over high heat. Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Add the garlic and spring onion whites and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rice and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming hot. Pour in the soy and sesame oil mixture and toss for 1 minute until evenly coloured.
Return the eggs, toss for 30 seconds, then stir through the spring onion greens and serve straight away.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers so the grains separate.
Toss the chicken with the salt and black pepper in a bowl.
Separate the white and green parts of the spring onions and keep them in two piles.
Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small jar or cup, ready to pour.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 30–40 seconds until just set and no longer runny.
Tip the eggs onto a plate and break into small pieces, then wipe out the wok.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil in the wok over high heat.
Add the chicken in a single layer and leave for 1 minute to brown, then stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre.
Add the garlic and spring onion whites and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Fry the rice and finish
steps: Add the rice to the wok and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes, pressing it against the wok, until steaming hot throughout and lightly toasted in places.
Pour the soy sauce and sesame oil mixture around the edge of the wok and toss for 1 minute until the rice is evenly coloured.
Return the eggs to the wok and toss for 30 seconds to combine.
Stir through the spring onion greens and serve straight away.

tips: Cold rice from the fridge is drier, so the grains fry and toast instead of turning mushy and clumping together.
Cutting the chicken into 1 cm pieces means it cooks through in the few minutes before the rice goes in.
Pouring the soy sauce around the hot edge of the wok makes it sizzle and caramelise slightly, adding a smoky flavour.
Frying in a single layer and keeping the heat high gives the browning that characterises chaufa; cook in two batches if your wok is small.
variations: Use 300 g peeled prawns instead of chicken and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque.
Add 1 tbsp finely grated ginger with the garlic for a sharper, more Chinese-Peruvian flavour.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot pan or microwave until steaming hot throughout. Do not reheat more than once.

title: Arroz caldo
summary: Comforting ginger chicken rice porridge with garlic, spring onions and a squeeze of calamansi or lime.
ingredients: 400 g chicken thigh, cut into 2 cm pieces
30 g ginger, cut into fine matchsticks
method: Rinse the rice and drain. Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat, then cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes until opaque on the outside.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock and 500 ml water. Bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to low and simmer, partly covered, for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the rice has broken down and thickened and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the fish sauce and pepper, loosening with a little hot water if too thick. Serve topped with the spring onions and the lime wedges.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1 minute, then drain well.
Cut the chicken thigh into 2 cm pieces, discarding any large pieces of fat.
Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic and cut the ginger into fine matchsticks.
Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the limes into wedges for serving.

stages.title: Soften the aromatics and brown the chicken
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 4 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the outside is opaque.

stages.title: Simmer the rice into porridge
steps: Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat the grains in the pan juices.
Pour in the chicken stock and 500 ml water, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 40 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to stop the rice sticking.
The porridge is ready when the grains have broken down and thickened, and the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside.

stages.title: Season and serve
steps: Stir in the fish sauce and black pepper.
If the porridge is thicker than you like, stir in up to 125 ml hot water and heat over low heat for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the spring onions, serving the lime wedges alongside.

tips: Rinsing the rice removes surface starch so the grains break down evenly rather than turning gluey at the bottom of the pot.
Chicken thigh stays tender through a long simmer, where breast would turn dry and stringy.
Stir regularly in the last 15 minutes, as the thickening porridge catches easily on the base of the pot.
Add the fish sauce at the end so its flavour stays fresh and you can judge the saltiness after the stock has reduced.
variations: Top with fried garlic and a halved boiled egg for a more traditional street-food style bowl.
Replace half the water with extra stock and add a pinch of saffron threads with the rice for the golden colour used in some versions.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. The porridge thickens as it cools, so reheat with a splash of water or stock until piping hot.

title: Atakilt wat
summary: Tender cabbage, potatoes and carrots simmered with turmeric, ginger and gentle Ethiopian spices.
ingredients: 500 g cabbage, cut into wide strips
400 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Cut the cabbage into wide strips, and cube the potatoes and carrots. Finely dice the onion and chop the garlic; grate the ginger.
Heat the oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat. Cook the onion with the salt for 8 minutes until soft and translucent, not browned.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the potatoes and carrots to coat.
Add 150 ml water, simmer gently, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the vegetables just soften at the edges.
Stir in the cabbage and black pepper, cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes until the potato is tender and the cabbage is soft.
Uncover and cook over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until the excess liquid evaporates. Season to taste and serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the cabbage into wide strips, discarding the tough core.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes; cut the carrots into thick half-moons.
Finely dice the onion, finely chop the garlic and grate the ginger.

stages.title: Soften the onion and spices
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep frying pan or wide pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and the salt and cook, stirring often, for 8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to scorch the spices.

stages.title: Cook the potatoes and carrots
steps: Add the potatoes and carrots to the pan and stir to coat in the spiced onion.
Pour in 150 ml water, bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cover with a lid.
Cook for 12 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the vegetables are just starting to soften at the edges.

stages.title: Add the cabbage and finish
steps: Add the cabbage on top, season with the black pepper and stir through; it will fill the pan at first and collapse as it cooks.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potato is tender when pierced with a knife and the cabbage is soft.
Remove the lid and cook for 2–3 minutes over medium heat until any excess liquid has evaporated.
Taste, add more salt if needed and serve warm.

tips: Cooking the onion slowly without browning gives the sweet, mild base that this turmeric-yellow dish depends on.
Cutting the potatoes and carrots smaller than the cabbage lets them cook through in the same time and keeps their shape.
Cooking the turmeric for only 30 seconds avoids a bitter, scorched flavour.
variations: Add 1 sliced capsicum with the cabbage for extra sweetness and colour.
Stir in 1/2 tsp ground cumin with the turmeric for a warmer, earthier flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until hot; the potato will be softer after reheating.

title: Fatteh
summary: Crisp pita layered with warm chickpeas, garlicky yoghurt, toasted pine nuts and lemon.
ingredients: 2 pita bread, torn into 3 cm pieces
2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Toss the torn pita with the olive oil on a tray and bake 8–10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic, 2 tbsp lemon juice and half the salt until smooth. Add more lemon juice if you want it sharper.
Simmer the chickpeas in a saucepan over medium heat with 125 ml water, the cumin and remaining salt for 5–6 minutes, until hot and mostly reduced.
Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium-low heat. Cook the pine nuts 2–3 minutes until golden brown, then remove from the heat.
Layer the pita, warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid in 4 bowls. Top with the yoghurt and pine nut butter, scatter with the parsley and serve.

stages.title: Toast the pita
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Spread the torn pita on a baking tray and toss with the olive oil.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp, then set aside.

stages.title: Make the garlic yoghurt
steps: Combine the yoghurt, garlic, 2 tbsp of the lemon juice and half the salt in a bowl.
Stir until smooth, taste, and add a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Warm the chickpeas
steps: Put the chickpeas in a saucepan with 125 ml water, the cumin and the remaining salt.
Heat over medium heat for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot and the liquid has mostly reduced.
Keep warm over the lowest heat.

stages.title: Brown the pine nuts
steps: Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the pine nuts and cook, stirring constantly, for 2–3 minutes until golden brown.
Remove from the heat straight away, as they scorch quickly.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Divide the toasted pita between 4 shallow bowls.
Spoon the warm chickpeas and a little of their liquid over the pita.
Top with the garlic yoghurt, then spoon the hot pine nut butter over the top.
Scatter with the parsley and serve immediately.

tips: Toasting the pita until fully crisp stops it turning to mush under the chickpeas and yoghurt.
Keep the pine nuts over medium-low heat and stir constantly, because the butter's milk solids and the nuts burn quickly and turn bitter.
Spooning some of the chickpea liquid over the pita softens the edges slightly while the centres stay crunchy.
Use full-fat yoghurt at room temperature so it stays creamy and doesn't cool the warm chickpeas too much.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp tahini into the yoghurt for a nuttier, richer sauce.
Replace the pine nuts with slivered almonds, browned the same way, if you prefer.
storage: Assembled fatteh goes soggy, so serve it straight away. Store leftover chickpeas and garlic yoghurt separately in the fridge for up to 2 days, and the pita in an airtight container. Reheat the chickpeas until piping hot.

title: Badrijani nigvzit
summary: Thin fried aubergine rolls filled with fragrant walnut, garlic and coriander paste.
method: Slice the eggplants lengthways into 5 mm strips, sprinkle both sides with the salt and leave for 20 minutes. Rinse briefly and pat very dry.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the strips in batches, 2–3 minutes each side until soft and golden, adding the remaining oil as needed.
Blitz the walnuts, garlic and coriander to a fine paste. Add the vinegar and 2–3 tbsp water until smooth but thick, then stir in half the parsley.
Drain the strips and let them cool in a single layer for 10 minutes, until cool to the touch.
Spread each strip with about 1 tbsp of paste, roll up from the narrow end and place seam side down. Scatter with the remaining parsley and the pomegranate seeds, if using.

stages.title: Slice and salt the eggplant
steps: Trim the eggplants and slice them lengthways into 5 mm strips.
Arrange the strips in a single layer on trays and sprinkle both sides with the salt.
Leave for 20 minutes to draw out moisture and bitterness.
Rinse the strips briefly and pat them very dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Fry the eggplant
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the strips in batches for 2–3 minutes each side, until soft and golden brown, adding the remaining 2 tbsp oil a little at a time as needed.
Drain the fried strips on paper towel.

stages.title: Make the walnut paste
steps: Blitz the walnuts, garlic and ground coriander in a food processor to a fine, crumbly paste.
Add the vinegar and 2–3 tbsp water, and blend until the paste is smooth and spreadable but still thick.
Stir in half the parsley.

stages.title: Cool the eggplant
steps: Spread the fried strips on a tray in a single layer.
Leave for 10 minutes, until completely cool to the touch.

stages.title: Fill and serve
steps: Spread about 1 tbsp of walnut paste over each cooled eggplant strip, leaving the ends clear.
Roll each strip up from the narrow end and place seam side down on a platter.
Scatter with the remaining parsley and the pomegranate seeds, if using, and serve at room temperature.

tips: Salting and drying the slices stops them soaking up oil, so they fry golden instead of greasy.
Cool the strips fully before spreading, or the warm eggplant makes the walnut paste oily and it slides out when rolled.
Add the water to the paste a spoonful at a time; too much makes it too loose to stay inside the rolls.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the walnut paste for a gentle heat.
Replace the parsley with coriander for a sharper herbal flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days; bring to room temperature before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Ochazuke
summary: Steamed rice bathed in hot green tea with salmon flakes, nori and sesame.
ingredients: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
method: Season the salmon with the salt. Cook in the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat, skin-side down for 4–5 minutes until crisp, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes until the flesh flakes easily.
Remove the skin and bones from the salmon, then flake the flesh into large pieces.
Slice the spring onions and nori thinly. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until lightly golden.
Microwave the rice, covered, for 2–3 minutes until steaming hot, then divide among four bowls.
Heat the green tea with the soy sauce in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Top the rice with the salmon, spring onions, nori and sesame seeds, then pour over the hot tea and serve.

stages.title: Cook the salmon
steps: Pat the salmon fillets dry and season both sides with the salt.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the salmon skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh flakes easily.
Lift the salmon onto a plate, remove the skin and any bones, then flake the flesh into large pieces.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings and rice
steps: Thinly slice the spring onions and cut the nori into thin strips with scissors.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry small frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking often, until lightly golden.
Warm the cooked rice in the microwave in a covered bowl for 2–3 minutes, until steaming hot, then divide among four bowls.

stages.title: Make the tea broth and serve
steps: Heat 500 ml of brewed green tea in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.
Stir the soy sauce into the tea.
Top the rice with the flaked salmon, spring onions, nori and sesame seeds.
Pour the hot tea around the rice, dividing it evenly among the bowls, and serve straight away.

tips: Heat the tea until steaming but not boiling, because boiling water makes green tea bitter and dulls its flavour.
Crisping the salmon skin and flaking the fish into large pieces keeps it from dissolving in the hot tea.
Pour the tea around the rice rather than over it so the nori stays crisp for the first few bites.
variations: Swap the salmon for 4 tbsp of shredded cooked chicken breast or a drained can of tuna.
Add 1 tsp of wasabi, stirred into the tea, for a sharper, hotter broth.

title: Polenta con funghi
summary: Creamy Parmesan polenta topped with buttery mushrooms, garlic and thyme.
method: Slice the mushrooms, chop the garlic, pick the thyme leaves and finely grate the parmesan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms in batches for 6–8 minutes, until deep golden and dry.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Season with half the salt and the pepper, then cover to keep warm off the heat.
Bring the stock and remaining salt to the boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and whisk in the polenta in a thin stream.
Cook for 3–5 minutes until thick and pulling away from the pan. Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter and the parmesan until smooth.
Spoon the polenta into warmed bowls and top with the mushrooms, pan juices and extra pepper.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Slice the mushrooms thickly, leaving small ones whole.
Finely chop the garlic and pick the thyme leaves from the sprigs.
Finely grate the parmesan.

stages.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps: Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook for 6–8 minutes without stirring too often, until deep golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Add the garlic and thyme leaves and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season with half the salt and a generous grind of black pepper, then cover to keep warm off the heat.

stages.title: Cook the polenta
steps: Pour the vegetable stock and the remaining salt into a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and slowly pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Cook, stirring with a wooden spoon, for 3–5 minutes or according to the packet, until thick and pulling away from the side of the pan.
Remove from the heat and stir in the remaining butter and the parmesan until melted and smooth.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Spoon the hot polenta into four warmed bowls.
Top with the mushrooms and any pan juices, and finish with extra black pepper.

tips: Mushrooms release a lot of water, so a wide pan and high heat let it evaporate and the mushrooms brown instead of steaming.
Pour the polenta in a slow stream while whisking so the grains separate and hydrate evenly, avoiding lumps.
Polenta thickens quickly as it stands, so stir in a splash of hot stock or water if it firms up before serving.
Mixed mushrooms such as Swiss brown, oyster and shiitake give more varied flavour and texture than one type.
variations: Stir 100 g gorgonzola or other blue cheese through the polenta with the parmesan for a stronger, tangier finish.
Finish the mushrooms with 2 tbsp white wine, simmered for 1 minute until almost evaporated, for extra depth.
storage: Refrigerate the polenta and mushrooms separately in covered containers for up to 2 days. Reheat the polenta in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water or stock, stirring until smooth and hot, and reheat the mushrooms until steaming.

title: Mast o khiar
summary: Cool thick yoghurt with diced cucumber, mint, walnuts and a hint of dried rose.
method: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for about 3 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Cool, then roughly chop.
Finely dice the cucumbers and toss with the salt in a sieve. Drain for 5 minutes, then press and pat dry. Roughly chop the sultanas.
Stir the yoghurt until smooth, then mix in the dried mint (rubbed between your palms) and the garlic.
Fold through the cucumber, sultanas and two-thirds of the walnuts.
Cover and chill for 25 minutes. Add a pinch more salt if needed.
Top with the remaining walnuts and the rose petals just before serving.

stages.title: Toast the walnuts
steps: Heat a small dry frying pan over medium heat.
Add the walnuts and toast for 3 minutes, stirring often, until fragrant and lightly golden.
Tip onto a plate and cool for 3 minutes, then roughly chop.

stages.title: Prepare the cucumber and sultanas
steps: Finely dice the cucumbers, then toss with the salt in a sieve set over a bowl.
Leave to drain for 5 minutes, then press gently and pat dry with paper towel so the yoghurt stays thick.
Roughly chop the sultanas so they spread evenly through the dip.

stages.title: Mix the yoghurt
steps: Spoon the greek yoghurt into a serving bowl and stir until smooth.
Rub the dried mint between your palms as you add it, then stir in the garlic.
Fold through the drained cucumber, the sultanas and two-thirds of the walnuts.

stages.title: Chill and serve
steps: Cover and refrigerate for 25 minutes so the mint softens and the flavours blend.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Scatter the remaining walnuts and the rose petals over the top just before serving.

tips: Salting and draining the cucumber removes water that would otherwise thin the yoghurt as it sits.
Rubbing dried mint between your palms warms it and releases its aroma.
Toast the walnuts to bring out their flavour and keep them crisp against the creamy yoghurt.
variations: Swap the sultanas for finely chopped dried apricots for a tarter sweetness.
Thin with 1/4 cup cold water and chill to serve as a cold soup over ice, in the style of a summer Persian soup.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 2 days. Stir before serving, as a little liquid may separate. Not suitable to freeze.

title: Upma
summary: Fluffy savoury semolina cooked with mustard seeds, curry leaves, vegetables and lemon.
method: Dice the onion and carrot finely, juice the lemon, and measure out the peas, semolina and water.
Toast the semolina in a large, deep frying pan over low-medium heat for 4–5 minutes until nutty and slightly darker. Tip into a bowl.
Heat the oil in the same pan over medium heat. Cook the mustard seeds until they pop, then add the curry leaves for 10 seconds.
Add the onion, carrot and salt and cook for 4–5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the water and peas and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce to low, pour in the semolina in a slow stream, then cover and cook 2–3 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Stir in the lemon juice, fluff with a fork and serve hot.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Finely dice the onion and carrot into pieces about 5 mm.
Juice the lemon and measure out the frozen peas.
Measure the semolina and the water so everything is within reach of the stove.

stages.title: Toast the semolina
steps: Heat a large, deep frying pan over low-medium heat and add the semolina without any oil.
Stir constantly for 4–5 minutes until it smells nutty and looks slightly darker, but has not browned.
Tip the semolina into a bowl and wipe out the pan.

stages.title: Cook the flavour base
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Add the mustard seeds and cook for 30–60 seconds until they pop, then add the curry leaves and stir for 10 seconds (they will spit).
Add the onion, carrot and salt and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.

stages.title: Cook the upma
steps: Pour in the 500 ml water, add the peas and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and pour in the toasted semolina in a slow stream, stirring constantly so no lumps form.
Cover and cook for 2–3 minutes until the water is absorbed and the semolina is soft and fluffy.
Stir in the lemon juice, fluff with a fork and serve hot.

tips: Toasting the semolina dry keeps the grains separate and fluffy instead of pasty.
Add the semolina in a slow stream while stirring, as pouring it in at once forms lumps that will not break down.
Dice the carrot very finely so it softens in the short cooking time.
variations: Add 1 tbsp roasted cashews with the mustard seeds for crunch.
Stir in 1 finely chopped red chilli with the onion for a spicier upma.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat with a splash of water in a pan or microwave until piping hot.

title: Yaki onigiri
summary: Grilled rice triangles with crisp soy-glazed surfaces and tender centres.
method: Spread the warm rice on a tray for 5 minutes until easy to handle but still sticky. Mix through the salt and sesame seeds.
With wet hands, divide the rice into 8 portions of about 75 g. Press each into a firm triangle about 2 cm thick, with no cracks.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil together in a small bowl for the glaze. Keep it and a pastry brush by the stove.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook 4 onigiri for 4–5 minutes each side, until golden, crisp and releasing easily.
Brush both sides with glaze, cooking 30 seconds per side until it sizzles and darkens. Repeat with the remaining oil and onigiri.

stages.title: Season the rice
steps: Spread the warm rice on a tray and leave it for 5 minutes, until it is comfortable to handle but still sticky.
Sprinkle the salt over the rice and mix it through with a rice paddle or spoon, then fold through the sesame seeds.

stages.title: Shape the triangles
steps: Wet your hands with cold water so the rice does not stick.
Divide the rice into 8 equal portions of about 75 g each.
Cup one portion in your palm and press it firmly into a compact triangle about 2 cm thick, turning and pressing until the grains hold together with no cracks.
Repeat with the remaining portions, rewetting your hands as needed.

stages.title: Make the glaze
steps: Stir the soy sauce, mirin and sesame oil together in a small bowl.
Set the bowl and a pastry brush next to the stove so the glaze is ready when the onigiri are crisp.

stages.title: Grill the onigiri
steps: Heat half the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add 4 onigiri and cook for 4–5 minutes on each side, without moving them, until golden and crisp and they release easily from the pan.
Brush the top of each with some of the glaze, turn and cook for 30 seconds until the glaze sizzles and darkens.
Brush the other side, turn again and cook for 30 seconds more, then remove to a plate.

Wipe the pan, heat the remaining vegetable oil over medium heat for 1 minute, then cook the remaining 4 onigiri for 4–5 minutes each side until golden and crisp, glazing them the same way for 30 seconds per side until the glaze darkens.

tips: Shape the rice while it is still warm, as the starch is stickiest then and the triangles hold together in the pan.
Leave the onigiri undisturbed while the first side crisps; moving them early tears the crust and they fall apart.
Brush the glaze on only at the end because the sugar in mirin burns quickly over direct heat.
variations: Press a teaspoon of miso paste mixed with a little mirin into the centre of each triangle before shaping for a salty filling.
Skip the glaze and brush the crisped onigiri with 1 tbsp miso paste thinned with 1 tbsp mirin instead.
storage: Refrigerate cooled onigiri in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes each side until hot through.

title: Calabacitas
summary: Tender courgette and sweetcorn sautéed with tomatoes, onion and mild green chilli.
ingredients: 1 red chilli, finely chopped (seeded for less heat)
method: Dice the zucchini, tomatoes, onion and chilli. Rinse frozen corn in a sieve under warm water to thaw, then drain well.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook the zucchini with the salt for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges and just tender.
Add the corn and tomatoes and cook for 3–4 minutes until the tomatoes soften and release their juices but the zucchini holds its shape.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Scatter the feta and coriander over and serve straight away.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut the zucchini into 1.5 cm dice so the pieces cook at the same rate.
Dice the tomatoes and finely chop the onion and chilli.
If using frozen corn, tip it into a sieve and rinse under warm water to thaw, then drain well.

stages.title: Soften the onion and chilli
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 4–5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the chilli and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Cook the zucchini and corn
steps: Increase the heat to medium-high, add the zucchini and the salt, and cook, stirring every minute, for 5–6 minutes until golden at the edges and just tender.
Add the corn and tomatoes and cook, stirring, for 3–4 minutes until the tomatoes have softened and released their juices but the zucchini still holds its shape.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Transfer to a serving dish and scatter over the feta and coriander.
Serve straight away while the zucchini is still tender.

tips: Dicing the zucchini evenly and cooking it over medium-high heat browns the edges and stops it steaming into mush.
Salt goes in with the zucchini so it draws out some moisture, which concentrates the flavour and helps the pieces colour.
Add the tomatoes late because long cooking breaks them down and makes the dish watery.
Feta is saltier than traditional queso fresco, so taste before adding extra salt at the end.
variations: Add 1 diced capsicum with the zucchini for extra sweetness and colour.
Stir through 2 tbsp sour cream at the end for a creamier version.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until hot; the zucchini will be softer than when fresh.

title: Semolina gnocchi alla romana
summary: Golden baked semolina rounds enriched with butter and Parmesan, crisp on top and tender inside.
method: Grease a 20 x 30 cm tray with a little of the 40 g butter and line it with baking paper. Split the parmesan into two 45 g portions and lightly whisk the egg yolks.
Heat the milk and salt in a large saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until steaming. Reduce to low and whisk in the semolina in a slow stream.
Stir for 8–10 minutes until very thick and pulling away from the pan sides. Off the heat, beat in 30 g butter, the egg yolks and half the parmesan until glossy.
Spread onto the tray 1.5 cm thick, cool for 15 minutes, then chill for 30 minutes until completely firm.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut into 5 cm rounds and overlap them in a greased baking dish, pressing trimmings into any gaps.
Dot with the remaining butter, scatter over the remaining parmesan and bake 20–25 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

stages.title: Prepare the tray and cheese
steps: Cut the butter into two portions: 30 g to stir into the semolina and 40 g for greasing and topping.
Use a little of the 40 g butter to grease a 20 x 30 cm tray, then line the base with baking paper.
Finely grate the parmesan and divide it into two equal portions of 45 g.
Lightly whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl.

stages.title: Cook the semolina
steps: Heat the milk and salt in a large saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Reduce the heat to low and whisk in the semolina in a slow, steady stream to avoid lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon and stir for 8–10 minutes until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Remove from the heat and beat in the 30 g butter, the egg yolks and 45 g of the parmesan until smooth and glossy.

stages.title: Spread and set
steps: Scrape the mixture onto the prepared tray and spread it to an even 1.5 cm thickness, smoothing the top with a wet spatula.
Cool for 15 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate for 30 minutes until completely firm to the touch.

stages.title: Cut the rounds
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut the set semolina into rounds with a 5 cm cutter, dipping it in water between cuts.
Grease a 20 x 30 cm baking dish with a little of the remaining butter.
Overlap the rounds in the dish, including the trimmings pressed into any gaps.

stages.title: Bake until golden
steps: Dot the remaining butter over the rounds and scatter over the remaining 45 g parmesan.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the tops are golden and the edges are crisp and bubbling.
Rest in the dish for 5 minutes before serving so the rounds hold their shape.

tips: Whisk the semolina in slowly while the milk is hot but not boiling, because dumping it in at once makes lumps that won't beat out.
Chill the mixture until fully firm so the rounds cut cleanly and don't slump or melt into one another when baked.
Dip the cutter in water between cuts so the sticky semolina releases without tearing.
Pressing the trimmings into the gaps means nothing is wasted and the top bakes into an even golden crust.
variations: Add a pinch of ground nutmeg with the egg yolks for a classic warm, nutty note.
Lay a few sage leaves between the rounds before baking, and scatter over extra browned butter to serve.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15 minutes until piping hot and crisp on top.

title: Cá kho tộ (caramelised fish)
summary: Tender fish steaks braised in caramelised fish sauce with black pepper and spring onion.
ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets, firm-fleshed, cut into 4 cm thick pieces
method: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and pat dry. Chop the garlic and shallots, and slice the spring onions and chilli for serving.
Heat the oil in a small heavy-based saucepan or clay pot over medium heat, add the sugar and cook for 4–5 minutes until deep amber.
Stir in the garlic and shallots for 1 minute until fragrant. Carefully add the water (it spits), stir until the caramel dissolves, then add the fish sauce.
Simmer over medium-low heat. Add the fish in a single layer and cook 6 minutes, then turn and cook 5–6 minutes more until cooked through and flaking. Cook the rice to packet directions meanwhile.
Lift out the fish and keep warm. Boil the sauce over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes until syrupy, then return the fish for 1 minute to coat.
Top with the pepper, spring onions and chilli, and serve with the rice.

stages.title: Prepare the fish and aromatics
steps: Cut the fish into 4 cm thick pieces and pat dry with paper towel.
Finely chop the garlic and shallots.
Thinly slice the spring onions and the red chilli, and keep them separate for serving.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Heat the oil in a small heavy-based saucepan or clay pot over medium heat, then add the sugar.
Cook without stirring, swirling the pan occasionally, for 4–5 minutes until the sugar melts to a deep amber colour.
Add the garlic and shallots and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stand back and carefully pour in the water, as it will spit. Stir for 1–2 minutes until the caramel dissolves, then stir in the fish sauce.

stages.title: Simmer the fish
steps: Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Nestle the fish pieces into the sauce in a single layer and cook, uncovered, for 6 minutes.
Turn the fish carefully and cook for 5–6 minutes more, spooning sauce over, until the fish flakes easily and is cooked through.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet.

stages.title: Reduce and serve
steps: Lift the fish onto a plate and cover loosely to keep warm.
Increase the heat to medium-high and boil the sauce for 3–4 minutes until syrupy and glossy.
Return the fish to the pan and spoon the sauce over for 1 minute to coat.
Sprinkle with the pepper, spring onions and chilli, and serve with the rice.

tips: Stop caramelising at deep amber, not dark brown; burnt sugar turns the sauce bitter.
Firm fish holds together during simmering, whereas delicate fillets can break up in the pan.
Use a small pan so the fish sits in the sauce; a wide pan makes the sauce reduce too quickly and leaves the fish dry.
Pouring the water into the hot caramel makes it spit, so add it slowly with the pan held away from you.
variations: Swap the fish for 600 g chicken thigh pieces and simmer for 20–25 minutes until cooked through with no pink inside.
Add 1 tbsp finely grated ginger with the garlic for a sharper, warmer flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot.

title: Espinacas con garbanzos
summary: Chickpeas and spinach simmered with smoky paprika, cumin and a garlic-bread thickener.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
2 slices bread, stale or day-old, torn into pieces
method: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Fry the torn bread for 2–3 minutes until golden, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant and pale golden.
Tip the bread and garlic into a small blender, leaving the oil in the pan. Blend with the paprika, cumin, red wine vinegar and 100 ml stock for 1 minute until a thick, mostly smooth paste forms.
Return the pan to medium heat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the chickpeas. Add the remaining 150 ml stock and simmer for 8 minutes until reduced by about half.
Stir in the paste and the salt, and cook for 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the chickpeas.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, stirring until wilted, about 3–4 minutes. Simmer 2 minutes more until no watery liquid pools.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve hot with the lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then leave them in the colander to drain well.
Tear the bread into rough 2 cm pieces and thinly slice the garlic.
Wash the baby spinach if needed and dry it well.
Cut the lemon into wedges.

stages.title: Fry the bread and garlic
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the bread, stirring often, for 2–3 minutes until golden all over.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant and pale golden, taking care it doesn't burn.
Tip the bread and garlic into a small blender, leaving the oil in the pan.

stages.title: Make the picada paste
steps: Add the paprika, ground cumin, red wine vinegar and 100 ml of the stock to the blender.
Blend for 1 minute until a thick, mostly smooth paste forms, scraping down the sides once.

stages.title: Simmer the chickpeas
steps: Return the pan to medium heat with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and add the chickpeas. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in the remaining 150 ml stock and simmer for 8 minutes until the liquid has reduced by about half.
Stir in the bread paste and the salt, and cook for 3 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings to the chickpeas.

stages.title: Wilt the spinach and serve
steps: Add the spinach a handful at a time over medium heat, stirring each batch in until it wilts before adding the next, about 3–4 minutes in total.
Simmer for 2 minutes more until the sauce is thick and no watery liquid pools.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, and serve hot with the lemon wedges.

tips: Stale bread soaks up the oil and thickens the sauce; fresh bread turns gluey, so dry it in a low oven if needed.
Fry the garlic only until pale golden, as browned garlic turns bitter and will dominate the paste.
Add the spinach in batches so the pan stays hot and the leaves wilt rather than stew and release excess water.
The red wine vinegar brightens the earthy chickpeas and cuts through the richness of the fried bread.
variations: Add 100 g diced chorizo, fried in the pan before the chickpeas, for a smoky meaty version.
Stir through a handful of toasted pine nuts and sultanas at the end for a Sevillan-style finish.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water or stock until piping hot. Does not freeze well because of the spinach.

title: Gyeran jjim
summary: Cloudlike steamed eggs with spring onions, gently cooked until soft and trembling.
method: Cool the stock if warm. Gently whisk the eggs, then mix in the stock, fish sauce and salt.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a heatproof 1 litre bowl and skim off any bubbles. Cover loosely with foil.
Set a rack in a wide pot with water 3 cm below it. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Lower in the bowl, cover the pot and steam for 12–15 minutes, until the surface is set with only a slight centre wobble.
Rest the custard for 2 minutes. Top with the sliced spring onions and sesame oil, and serve hot.

stages.title: Make the egg mixture
steps: Let the vegetable stock cool to room temperature if it is warm, as hot stock will scramble the eggs.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk gently with a fork until the whites and yolks are combined, without creating foam.
Stir in the cooled stock, fish sauce and salt until evenly mixed.
Pour the mixture through a fine sieve into a heatproof 1 litre bowl, then skim off any surface bubbles with a spoon.
Thinly slice the spring onions and set them aside.

stages.title: Set up the steamer
steps: Place a steaming rack or upturned heatproof saucer in a large wide pot and add water to reach 3 cm below the rack.
Bring the water to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low so it simmers barely.
Cover the bowl of egg mixture loosely with foil, leaving a small gap for steam to escape.

stages.title: Steam the custard
steps: Carefully lower the covered bowl onto the rack, put the lid on the pot and steam over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes.
Check at 12 minutes by gently shaking the bowl: the custard is ready when the surface is set and the centre has only a slight wobble, with no liquid egg when pressed lightly with a spoon.
If the centre is still liquid, re-cover and steam for 2–3 minutes more, then check again.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Turn off the heat and lift the bowl out with oven mitts, taking care with the hot steam.
Rest the custard for 2 minutes so it finishes setting.
Scatter the spring onions over the top, drizzle with the sesame oil and serve hot in the bowl.

tips: Straining the egg mixture removes the stringy egg white, which gives a smooth, even custard.
Keep the water at a barely-there simmer, because a hard boil makes the custard curdle and develop holes.
Loose foil stops condensation dripping onto the surface and leaving pockmarks.
Whisk gently without foaming the eggs, as bubbles turn into a spongy texture when steamed.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp finely grated carrot into the egg mixture for extra sweetness and colour.
Add 1 tsp kimchi juice or a pinch of chilli flakes to the egg mixture for a gentle kick.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently in the microwave on medium for 30–60 seconds, until just warm.

title: Farofa
summary: Toasted cassava flour with buttery onions and bacon for a crunchy savoury accompaniment.
method: Cook the bacon in a large frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until golden and crisp. Lift it out onto a plate, leaving the fat in the pan.
Add the butter to the bacon fat over medium heat. When it foams, add the onion and cook for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Reduce to medium-low, add the cassava flour and stir constantly for 4–5 minutes, until golden and sandy with no raw floury smell.
Stir in the bacon, parsley, salt and a few grinds of pepper. Taste, adjust the salt and serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Finely dice the bacon and finely chop the onion.
Finely chop the parsley and set it aside.
Measure the cassava flour into a bowl so it is ready to add.

stages.title: Crisp the bacon
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the bacon to the dry pan.
Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until the fat has rendered and the bacon is golden and crisp.
Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.

stages.title: Soften the onion
steps: Return the pan to medium heat and add the butter to the bacon fat.
When the butter has melted and is foaming, add the onion.
Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned.

stages.title: Toast the flour and finish
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the cassava flour to the pan.
Stir constantly for 4–5 minutes, until the flour is lightly toasted, golden and sandy, with no raw floury smell.
Stir in the bacon, the parsley, the salt and a few grinds of black pepper.
Taste and add more salt if needed, then serve warm.

tips: Use a large pan so the flour spreads thin and toasts evenly instead of steaming into clumps.
Keep the heat at medium-low once the flour goes in, because cassava flour scorches quickly and turns bitter.
Bacon is salty, so add the salt only at the end, after tasting.
variations: Stir in 2 chopped hard-boiled eggs with the parsley for a more traditional, heartier farofa.
Use 2 thinly sliced spring onions in place of the parsley for a sharper flavour.
storage: Cool completely and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until warm and crumbly again.

title: Bresaola rucola e grana
summary: Paper-thin cured beef layered with peppery rocket, Parmesan shavings and lemon.
method: Wash and thoroughly dry the rocket. Shave the parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler and chill them, along with four plates.
Zest the lemon, then juice it. Whisk 2 tbsp of the juice with the olive oil, black pepper and salt, and add more juice if you want it sharper.
Lay the bresaola in a single slightly overlapping layer on the chilled plates, 40 g per plate. Rest for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Toss the rocket with half the dressing until lightly coated, then pile it over the bresaola.
Top with the parmesan curls and lemon zest, drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve straight away.

stages.title: Prepare the rocket and cheese
steps: Wash the rocket, then dry it thoroughly in a salad spinner or between clean tea towels so the dressing clings.
Shave the parmesan into thin curls with a vegetable peeler and keep them in the fridge until serving.
Put four plates in the fridge to chill.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Zest the lemon finely, then juice it to get about 3 tbsp juice.
Whisk 2 tbsp lemon juice with the olive oil, black pepper and salt in a small bowl until combined.
Taste the dressing on a piece of rocket and add a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Arrange the bresaola
steps: Take the chilled plates from the fridge.
Lay the bresaola slices loosely across the plates in a single layer, slightly overlapping, using 40 g per plate.
Leave the slices to sit for 5 minutes at room temperature so the flavour softens and the slices separate easily.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Toss the rocket in a large bowl with half the dressing until lightly coated.
Pile the rocket over the bresaola on each plate.
Scatter the parmesan curls and lemon zest on top.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve straight away, before the rocket wilts.

tips: Dry rocket keeps the dressing from watering down and lets it cling to the leaves.
Chilled plates keep the thin bresaola cool and stop it going greasy as it sits.
Dress the rocket only at the last minute, because lemon juice wilts the leaves within minutes.
Shaving the cheese with a peeler gives wide, thin curls that melt on the tongue rather than crumbling.
variations: Add 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts over the top for crunch.
Replace the parmesan with shaved pecorino for a sharper, saltier flavour.

title: Melitzanosalata
summary: Smoky aubergine dip with lemon, garlic, parsley and fruity olive oil.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Prick the eggplants all over and roast on a lined tray for 40–45 minutes, turning once, until charred and completely soft.
Cool the eggplants for 10 minutes, then scoop the flesh into a fine sieve, discarding the skins. Drain for 15 minutes, pressing gently once or twice.
Roughly chop the flesh and combine in a bowl with the garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Stir in the olive oil a little at a time until creamy but still chunky, then fold through the parsley.
Rest covered at room temperature for 15 minutes, then taste and adjust the salt or lemon juice.
Warm the pita in the oven for 2–3 minutes if you like, and serve with the dip.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Prick each eggplant 6–8 times all over with a fork.
Roast the eggplants on the tray for 40–45 minutes, turning once halfway, until the skins are wrinkled and charred and the flesh is completely soft when pressed.

stages.title: Drain the flesh
steps: Leave the eggplants to cool for 10 minutes, until you can handle them.
Split them open and scoop the flesh into a fine sieve, discarding the skins.
Let the flesh drain for 15 minutes, pressing gently with a spoon once or twice to release the bitter liquid.

stages.title: Mix the salad
steps: Chop the drained flesh roughly on a board, keeping some texture.
Place it in a bowl with the garlic, lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Stir in the olive oil a little at a time until the mixture is creamy but still chunky.
Fold through the parsley.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Cover and rest the melitzanosalata at room temperature for 15 minutes so the garlic and lemon mellow into the eggplant.
Taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed.
Warm the pita in the oven for 2–3 minutes if you like, then serve with the dip.

tips: Pricking the skins lets steam escape so the eggplants don't burst in the oven.
Roasting until the skin is charred gives a smoky flavour; underbaked eggplant tastes bitter and stays stringy.
Draining the flesh stops the dip turning watery and diluting the lemon and garlic.
Adding the oil gradually helps it blend into the flesh for a creamier texture.
variations: Add 1 tbsp red wine vinegar in place of half the lemon juice for a sharper, more traditional taste.
Char the eggplants directly over a gas flame or barbecue, turning often for 15–20 minutes, for a stronger smoky flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 2 days. Bring to room temperature and stir before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Basbousa
summary: Tender semolina cake soaked in fragrant lemon syrup and topped with toasted almonds.
ingredients: 100 g butter, melted, plus extra for greasing
1 lemon, half juiced (about 2 tbsp) and the other half cut into 2 strips of peel
method: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 20 cm square tin with extra butter and line the base. Mix the semolina, caster sugar and baking powder.
Stir in the yoghurt and melted butter until just combined, then rest the batter for 5 minutes.
Spoon the batter into the tin and smooth the top. Cut into 12 pieces almost to the base and press an almond into each.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean.
Meanwhile, simmer the white sugar, water and lemon peel in a saucepan over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Stir in the lemon juice and discard the peel.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and re-cut the score lines. Leave in the tin for at least 1 hour, until cooled and the syrup is absorbed.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and grease a 20 cm square cake tin with a little extra butter, then line the base with baking paper.
In a large bowl, stir together the semolina, caster sugar and baking powder.
Add the yoghurt and the melted butter and stir until just combined into a thick, spoonable batter.
Rest the batter in the bowl for 5 minutes so the semolina absorbs some liquid.

stages.title: Shape and score
steps: Spoon the batter into the tin and smooth the top with a wet spatula.
Cut the batter into 12 diamonds or squares with a knife, cutting almost to the base.
Press one almond into the centre of each piece.

stages.title: Bake the cake
steps: Bake on the middle rack for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden on top and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
While the cake bakes, put the white sugar, water and lemon peel strips in a small saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Remove from the heat, stir in the lemon juice and discard the peel strips.

stages.title: Soak and rest
steps: Pour the warm syrup slowly and evenly over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven, while the cake is still hot.
Re-cut along the score lines if they have closed up.
Leave the cake in the tin for at least 1 hour, until it has absorbed the syrup and cooled, before lifting out the pieces.

tips: Pouring warm syrup over a hot cake lets the semolina soak it up evenly, so the pieces stay moist rather than soggy on the bottom.
Scoring before baking gives clean pieces, because the syrupy cake is too tender to cut neatly afterwards.
Resting the batter for 5 minutes softens the semolina grains, which gives a tender crumb instead of a gritty one.
variations: Replace the lemon juice in the syrup with 1 tsp orange blossom water if you have it, added once the syrup is off the heat.
Stir 3 tbsp desiccated coconut into the dry ingredients for a coconut basbousa.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Mercimek köfte (lentil köfte)
summary: Soft red lentil and bulgur patties seasoned with pepper paste, cumin and fresh herbs.
method: Rinse the red lentils, then boil them in 600 ml water with the salt over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and simmer 12–15 minutes until collapsed, thick and mushy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the bulgur, cover and leave 15 minutes until swollen and a firm paste.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion 6–7 minutes until soft and golden, then add the tomato paste and cumin and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Mix the onion mixture into the lentils, then add the spring onions, parsley and lemon juice. Mix with damp hands until it holds together when squeezed, then cool 5 minutes.
Shape heaped tablespoons into small ovals about 6 cm long, making about 20. Serve warm or at room temperature in the lettuce leaves.

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Place the lentils in a medium saucepan with 600 ml water and the salt, and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring often, for 12–15 minutes until the lentils have collapsed and the mixture is thick and mushy.
Take the pan off the heat.

stages.title: Hydrate the bulgur
steps: Stir the fine bulgur into the hot lentils until evenly combined.
Cover the pan with a lid and leave off the heat for 15 minutes, until the bulgur has swollen and absorbed the moisture and the mixture is a thick, firm paste.

stages.title: Make the onion base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the diced onion, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and ground cumin and cook for 1 minute until the paste darkens slightly and smells fragrant.

stages.title: Combine the mixture
steps: Scrape the onion mixture into the lentil and bulgur mixture and stir well.
Add the spring onions, parsley and lemon juice and mix, using damp hands, until the mixture is evenly coloured and holds together when squeezed.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes until comfortable to handle.

stages.title: Shape and serve
steps: With damp hands, take a heaped tablespoon of mixture, squeeze it in your fist and press into a small oval about 6 cm long, leaving finger marks.
Repeat with the remaining mixture to make about 20 kofte.
Arrange the kofte on a platter with the lettuce leaves and serve warm or at room temperature, wrapped in the leaves with a squeeze of extra lemon if you like.

tips: Fine bulgur softens in the lentils' residual heat without cooking, so you get a firm, shapeable paste rather than a wet one.
Shape the kofte with damp hands because the warm mixture sticks to dry ones.
Frying the tomato paste briefly removes its raw edge and deepens the colour and flavour.
variations: Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the cumin for a spicier kofte.
Stir 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses through the mixture with the lemon juice for a sweet-sour finish, if you have it.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days and serve cold or at room temperature. Freeze shaped kofte for up to 1 month and thaw in the fridge overnight.

title: Sunomono
summary: Cool cucumber ribbons dressed in sweet rice vinegar with sesame and delicate wakame seaweed.
method: Thinly slice the cucumbers, toss with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, until softened and watery.
Soak the wakame in 500 ml cold water for 5 minutes, until soft and fully expanded. Drain, squeeze dry and cut long pieces into bite-sized lengths.
Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar and soy sauce for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until lightly golden.
Rinse the cucumber, squeeze out as much liquid as you can, then toss gently with the wakame and dressing. Chill for 10 minutes.
Serve cold in small bowls, topped with the toasted sesame seeds.

stages.title: Salt the cucumber
steps: Slice the cucumbers as thinly as you can with a mandoline or sharp knife, then place in a bowl.
Sprinkle the cucumber with the salt and toss well.
Leave to stand for 10 minutes, until the cucumber softens and releases liquid.

stages.title: Rehydrate the wakame
steps: Place the wakame in a bowl and cover with 500 ml cold water.
Soak for 5 minutes, until soft, glossy and fully expanded.
Drain the wakame, squeeze out the excess water and cut any long pieces into bite-sized lengths.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Whisk the rice vinegar, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, shaking often, until lightly golden, then tip onto a plate.

stages.title: Dress and chill
steps: Rinse the cucumber under cold water to remove the surface salt, then squeeze small handfuls firmly to remove as much liquid as possible.
Combine the cucumber and wakame in a bowl, pour over the dressing and toss gently.
Cover and chill in the fridge for 10 minutes.
Serve cold in small bowls, sprinkled with the toasted sesame seeds.

tips: Salting draws water out of the cucumber, so it stays crisp and doesn't dilute the dressing.
Rinsing the salted cucumber before squeezing stops the dish tasting too salty.
Squeezing the wakame dry keeps the dressing sharp and balanced rather than watery.
Toasting the sesame seeds brings out their nutty flavour, which balances the tang of the vinegar.
variations: Add 100 g cooked and peeled prawns, tossed through with the dressing, for a seafood version.
Add 1 tsp finely grated ginger to the dressing for a sharper, warmer flavour.
storage: Best eaten within a few hours. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for up to 1 day; the cucumber will soften. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Dhokla
summary: Fluffy steamed chickpea cakes topped with mustard seeds, curry leaves and fresh coriander.
method: Sift the chickpea flour into a bowl, then whisk in the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar for 2 minutes until smooth. Rest 10 minutes. Oil a 20 cm cake tin.
Bring 3 cm water to the boil in a wide pot with a rack over high heat, then reduce to medium to keep it steadily simmering.
Whisk the fruit salt into the batter until frothy and paler. Pour into the tin, set on the rack, cover and steam 15–18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the dhokla in the tin for 10 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a board.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan over medium heat, then cook the mustard seeds until they pop. Add the curry leaves and chilli for 15 seconds.
Add 2 tbsp water and the remaining sugar, simmer 1 minute until dissolved. Spoon over the dhokla squares and scatter with the coriander.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour into a large bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar.
Whisk for 2 minutes until completely smooth and thick like pancake batter.
Brush a 20 cm round cake tin with 1 tbsp of the oil so the dhokla releases cleanly.

stages.title: Rest the batter and heat the steamer
steps: Cover the bowl and rest the batter for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Meanwhile, pour 3 cm water into a large wide pot with a rack and bring to the boil over high heat.
Lower the heat to medium so the water keeps simmering steadily.

stages.title: Steam the dhokla
steps: Whisk the fruit salt into the rested batter for 10 seconds until it turns frothy and slightly paler.
Pour the batter straight into the greased tin and set it on the rack in the pot.
Cover with a lid and steam over medium heat for 15–18 minutes, until the dhokla is risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Cool the dhokla
steps: Lift the hot tin out carefully and cool for 10 minutes so the cake firms up.
Run a knife around the edge and turn the dhokla out onto a board.

stages.title: Temper and serve
steps: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the mustard seeds and cook until they start to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the curry leaves and chilli and stir for 15 seconds.
Pour in 2 tbsp water and add the remaining sugar, then simmer for 1 minute until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the dhokla into squares, spoon the tempering over the top and scatter with the coriander.

tips: Add the fruit salt only just before steaming, because it reacts with the yoghurt straight away and the bubbles that make the dhokla light are lost if the batter waits.
Sifting the chickpea flour prevents lumps, which would steam into dense pockets.
Wrapping the pot lid in a clean tea towel stops condensation dripping onto the surface and leaving it soggy.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely grated ginger into the batter for a sharper, warmer flavour.
Replace the chilli in the tempering with 1 tsp sesame seeds for a milder, nutty finish.
storage: Refrigerate the dhokla in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a steamer or microwave for 1–2 minutes until hot, and add the tempering fresh if you can.

title: Tarte fine aux pommes
summary: Thin apple slices baked on crisp buttery puff pastry with a glossy apricot glaze.
ingredients: 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed (about 25 cm square)
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Lay the puff pastry on a lined tray, score a border 1.5 cm in and prick the centre with a fork.
Juice the lemon into a bowl. Thinly slice the apples (2–3 mm, skin on) and toss them in the juice.
Arrange the apples in overlapping rows inside the border. Brush with the melted butter and sprinkle with the caster sugar.
Bake on the middle shelf for 30 minutes, until the border is deep golden and the apple edges are browned. Cover loosely with foil if the apples brown too fast.
Meanwhile, warm the apricot jam with 1 tsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until runny. Brush it over the hot tart.
Rest the tart on the tray for 10 minutes, until the pastry firms up, then cut into 4 pieces.

stages.title: Prepare the pastry base
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Lay the puff pastry sheet on the tray.
Use a small sharp knife to score a border about 1.5 cm in from the edge, cutting only halfway through the pastry.
Prick the pastry inside the border all over with a fork so the centre doesn't puff up too much.

stages.title: Slice and arrange the apples
steps: Juice the lemon into a large bowl.
Halve and core the apples, leaving the skin on, then slice them very thinly (2–3 mm) and toss them in the lemon juice so they don't brown.
Arrange the apple slices in slightly overlapping rows inside the scored border, covering the pastry completely.
Brush the apples with the melted butter and sprinkle evenly with the caster sugar.

stages.title: Bake the tart
steps: Bake the tart on the middle shelf for 30 minutes, until the pastry border is puffed and deep golden and the apple edges are browned.
If the apples are browning faster than the pastry, cover the tart loosely with foil for the last 5–10 minutes.
Check that the pastry underneath is golden and crisp by lifting an edge with a spatula.

stages.title: Glaze the tart
